newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's Manh rules out elected leadership.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's Manh rules out elected leadership.

text.p: Vietnam's National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh said in an interview published on Monday that Hanoi wanted to encourage popular participation in politics but would not countenance direct elections for the leadership.

Manh, who ranks fourth in the elite politburo, spoke in vague terms to the Tuoi Tre newspaper about the need for the "direct mastery of the people" in matters concerning Vietnam's National Assembly, or single-party parliament.
He said draft revisions to the election rules would be discussed at the assembly's next session, due in March or April, and said people should be encouraged to monitor the activities of government.

"We are considering at this time how to better bring into play the mastery of the people (in decision making)," he said. "It is possible we could accept opinions on matters affecting the constitution and some laws."
But asked whether direct elections might be used to select the country's top leaders he indicated this was unnecessary.
"We have a party leadership system that ensures that those who are selected represent the people's views and have the confidence of the people," he replied.
Vietnam is ruled by a communist government in which policy decisions are made by an elite collective.

The National Assembly comprises representatives selected from across the country once every five years. Although traditionally seen as a rubber-stamp body, it has shown increased capacity for debate in recent years.
A new assembly is due to be selected later this year through an election process expected to be held on July 20.
